name: Jongmin Choi
title: MS Student in Multimodal AI
university: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)
bio:
I am an MS student in the Multimodal AI (MMAI) Lab at KAIST, advised by Professor Joon Son Chung. Biological intelligence is the clearest existence proof we have of a general and efficient learner, and I believe that networks shaped by its principles rather than by scale alone can become more capable and efficient.

My master's research has followed this belief in two directions. First, I studied the gap between audio and text and how multimodal models can narrow it while preserving the structure unique to each modality. Second, I asked what the basic unit of computation should be. A biological neuron is not simply a perceptron. It spikes, resets, and is shaped by its membrane channels, and I developed spiking neuron algorithms that place these mechanisms within the neuron itself.

I am now studying connectors between audio encoders and language-model decoders to reduce information bottlenecks, and in parallel I investigate the mathematical foundations of optimization algorithms for training deep networks. I am always open to discussing research ideas and potential collaborations, so please feel free to reach out!
